notes: Sign in with the generated password (OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD); Open Notebook has a single shared password, no user accounts. Every page and every API call needs it.

Only the web UI port (8502) is published. The browser reaches the REST API through the UI at https://<domain>/api: Next.js forwards /api/* to the API on port 5055 inside the same container (upstream's single-port reverse-proxy setup, docs/5-CONFIGURATION/reverse-proxy.md). API_URL is the site's HTTPS address, so the frontend never points the browser at port 5055. CORS_ORIGINS is the site's own origin (upstream's production advice); the browser only ever calls the API same-origin through the UI.

No AI provider ships with the recipe. Add one in Settings, Models (API key and model); keys are stored encrypted in the database with OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Upstream accepts any string as the key and derives the Fernet key from it with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, so the generated 32-character secret is used as is. Changing or losing it makes the saved provider keys unreadable.

The database is SurrealDB v2.7.0 (the v2 line upstream's compose and Dockerfile use), with a generated root user and password, on its own volume and with no published port. Upstream passes the root user and password as --user/--pass on the command line; this recipe passes them as SURREAL_USER and SURREAL_PASS in the container environment instead, because process arguments are readable by every account on the host and the database's container address is reachable from the host. It runs as root inside its container, as in upstream's compose, so it can write to the volume.

The data volume (/app/data) holds uploads, generated podcasts and caches. The optional heavy extraction runtimes (OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENABLE_DOCLING, OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENABLE_CRAWL4AI) are off; enabling them downloads large packages into that volume on the next start and needs a bigger memory limit.
The container's healthcheck checks both the API (/health on 5055) and the UI (8502), so the panel shows the app as running only once both answer.
